pos.personaBrief: Leverkusen controlled the ball (59% average possession in 2023/24, Coaches' Voice) but waited compactly vs Bayern (38%), so possession is the default, not a dogma.

pro.personaBrief: Slow, methodical build-up through a back three and a central pivot (Coaches' Voice 2022/23), turning Xhaka into a 100-pass metronome, though direct once in the opponent's half.

est.personaBrief: Positional play with defined phases and rotations (3-4-2-1 and 4-2-3-1 in possession), with central 10s and close associative combinations.

lar.personaBrief: Second-lowest crosses in the Bundesliga and a preference for progressing centrally, though wing-backs were placed very wide to stretch the block (SempreMilan).

blo.personaBrief: Moved from a mid-block to pressing from the start of build-up, with immediate counter-pressing and wing-backs jumping out; a hybrid press, compact when needed.

mar.personaBrief: Mixed-marking and one-to-one at the back against Bayern, with a hybrid press: man-oriented elements within a zonal frame.

pla.personaBrief: A clear game model retained across opponents, but flexible: a compact low block vs Bayern, and 'flexible and adaptable based on opponent quality'.

res.personaBrief: Aesthetic, proactive football in service of winning (unbeaten double); played to win rather than settle, while closing games smartly.

sis.personaBrief: System-first: nearly identical XI, roles tied to the model, players improved by it (Xhaka, Hincapie), everyone working in the press.

jog.personaBrief: Technical profile preferred: passing pivots like Xhaka, technical 10s (Wirtz), with pressing intensity required.

bas.personaBrief: Mix of a stable experienced core (Xhaka, Andrich) and young talents (Wirtz, Hincapie), with youngsters given minutes once the title was won; praises academy philosophy.

lid.personaBrief: Communicative, rewards sacrifice (Andrich) and rotates, but 'likes discipline' per Grimaldo; balanced leader with firm rules.
